newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA TO PROBE CHILAVERT CASE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA TO PROBE CHILAVERT CASE.

text.p: FIFA is to seek further details about a 13-month ban from Argentine soccer imposed on Paraguay captain Jose Luis Chilavert by a judge this week.

The extrovert goalkeeper was additionally given a three-month suspended jail sentence for punching a stadium assistant during a match between his Velez Sarsfield club and Gimnasia y Esgrima de la Plata in April 1994.
FIFA has always insisted sporting disciplinary action should be taken by the appropriate sporting body and a spokesman for the governing body said on Friday the Chilavert case would be examined.
"Apart from anything else, he's from Paraguay and is playing in Argentina which makes it an international issue," the spokesman said.

Chilavert, who scored from a free-kick against Argentina to clinch a draw for Paraguay in a World Cup qualifier in Buenos Aires on Sunday, has claimed he is being victimised because of his nationality.
"They can't forgive me my success because I'm Paraguayan, but I feel more proud of that than ever," he said.

A menacing figure in goal who wears a bulldog design on his chest and thrives on intimidating opposing players, Chilavert is a national hero in Paraguay and was decorated by its government just weeks ago for his soccer prowess.
Regarded by some as the best goalkeeper in the world, he helped his club win Argentina's last championship, saving a penalty in the match that clinched the title.
